positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described significant traumatic experiences involving threats to life and serious injury. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports sudden images and memories of the event, feeling overwhelmed and distressed. Criterion B2 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient actively tries to avoid thoughts and reminders of the trauma. Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids places and gatherings that could trigger memories. Criterion B4 (inability to recall details): MET — patient finds it challenging to remember specific details of the trauma. Criterion C1 (negative beliefs): NOT MET — patient indicated negativity is not constant and is triggered by specific events. Criterion C2 (self-blame): UNCLEAR — patient expresses blame but does not confirm it is constant or unreasonable. Criterion C3 (negative emotional state): NOT MET — patient does not report feelings as always negative. Criterion C4 (diminished interest): MET — patient reports decreased engagement in previously enjoyed activities. Criterion C5 (detachment): MET — patient experiences feelings of detachment from others. Criterion C6 (inability to experience positive emotions): MET — patient struggles to feel happy or satisfied. Criterion D1 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability and outbursts. Criterion D2 (recklessness): MET — patient describes being more reckless as a coping mechanism. Criterion D3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient feels more on edge and alert. Criterion D4 (startle response): MET — patient reports increased startle response. Criterion D5 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient has difficulty concentrating, especially when reminded of the trauma. Criterion D6 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient struggles with sleep, waking up suddenly with racing thoughts. Criterion E (duration): MET — symptoms began after the traumatic event and have lasted for more than one month. Criterion F (functional impairment): MET — patient reports significant distress and interference with work and social interactions. Exclusions: NOT TRIGGERED — patient denies substance use or other medical conditions contributing to symptoms. Total: Requires ≥1 from each cluster (B, C, D); found all criteria from B (4), C (4), and D (6) met. Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
